h: Terry Jones in your ear and pistols in the village
p: Here's a lovely touch for Python fans. The audio guide at Doune Castle is narrated by the late Terry Jones, one of the Monty Python team and co-director of Holy Grail. He shares the castle's real history along with a few memories from filming in the mid-1970s, so you get both sides of the story as you wander. Outlander fans get their bit too, with Sam Heughan, who plays Jamie Fraser, chipping in on the parts filmed here as Castle Leoch.

Don't rush off once you're back in the car park. The village of Doune has its own claim to fame: in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it was known for pistol-making, and Doune pistols were prized by Highland gentlemen. It's a nice little detail to share as you walk through the village.

An hour or two is enough for the castle itself, which leaves room for more. Deanston Distillery, a short hop away, is housed in an old cotton mill on the Teith and is a good stop for grown-ups (with a designated driver). Blair Drummond Safari Park is also close, which makes a brilliant combination if you've got kids who need something completely different after a medieval castle.
Dunblane, with its cathedral, and the Victorian spa town of Bridge of Allan are both a short drive away for food and a wander.
